# Verify line-fill hypothesis programmatically against demo.
import numpy as np
ar=np.array(A); br=np.array(B)
marked=np.zeros(ar.shape,bool)
for r in range(ar.shape[0]):
    inds=np.flatnonzero(ar[r]==6)
    for x,y in zip(inds,inds[1:]): marked[r,x:y+1]=True
for c in range(ar.shape[1]):
    inds=np.flatnonzero(ar[:,c]==6)
    for x,y in zip(inds,inds[1:]): marked[x:y+1,c]=True
pred=ar.copy(); pred[marked & (ar==1)]=3
print('match',np.array_equal(pred,br),'mismatches',[(tuple(x),int(pred[tuple(x)]),int(br[tuple(x)])) for x in np.argwhere(pred!=br)[:20]],'count',np.count_nonzero(pred!=br))

program='''def transform(grid):
    """Connect every pair of aligned marker cells with color 3."""
    out = [row[:] for row in grid]
    h = len(grid)
    w = len(grid[0]) if h else 0
    markers = sorted({v for row in grid for v in row if v != grid[0][0]})
    # In these puzzles, the non-background color is the marker (usually one value).
    if not markers:
        return out
    marker = markers[0]
    for r in range(h):
        xs = [c for c in range(w) if grid[r][c] == marker]
        for x, y in zip(xs, xs[1:]):
            for c in range(x + 1, y):
                if grid[r][c] != marker:
                    out[r][c] = 3
    for c in range(w):
        ys = [r for r in range(h) if grid[r][c] == marker]
        for x, y in zip(ys, ys[1:]):
            for r in range(x + 1, y):
                if grid[r][c] != marker:
                    out[r][c] = 3
    return out
'''
p.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
file.write_text(program)
